# Glossary {-}

```{=latex}
\markboth{Glossary}{Glossary}
```

**Absolute value.** The distance of a real number from zero on the number line.

**Average rate of change.** The ratio of net output change to input change over an interval.

**Completing the square.** Rewriting a quadratic by adding and subtracting the value needed to form a perfect-square trinomial.

**Composite function.** The function $(f\circ g)(x)=f(g(x))$, formed by using the output of $g$ as the input of $f$.

**Data matrix.** A rectangular arrangement in which rows represent cases and columns represent variables.

**Domain.** The set of inputs for which a function is defined.

**End behaviour.** The behaviour of a function as $x\to\infty$ and as $x\to-\infty$.

**Equation.** A statement that two expressions have equal values.

**Equivalent formula.** A rearranged equation that expresses the same relationship while isolating a different variable.

**Exponent.** A number that indicates the power to which a base is raised.

**Exponential function.** A function $f(x)=ab^x$, where $a\ne0$, $b>0$, and $b\ne1$.

**Factor.** An expression multiplied by another expression to produce a given product.

**Fraction.** A quotient $a/b$ in which $a$ is the numerator, $b$ is the denominator, and $b\ne0$.

**Fractional expression.** A quotient of two algebraic expressions, with all values that make the denominator zero excluded.

**Function.** A rule that assigns exactly one output to every input in its domain.

**Hole.** A removable discontinuity created when a common factor cancels but its zero remains excluded from the original domain.

**Horizontal asymptote.** A line $y=L$ approached by a function as $x\to\infty$ or $x\to-\infty$.

**Increasing function.** A function whose outputs rise as inputs increase on a specified interval.

**Inequality.** A comparison between quantities using $<$, $\le$, $>$, or $\ge$.

**Interquartile range.** The spread of the middle half of the data, $IQR=Q_3-Q_1$.

**Interval.** A continuous set of real numbers between specified endpoints.

**Inverse function.** A function $f^{-1}$ that reverses a one-to-one function, so $f^{-1}(f(x))=x$ on the domain of $f$.

**Inverse sine.** The function $\arcsin:[-1,1]\to[-\pi/2,\pi/2]$ satisfying $\sin(\arcsin x)=x$.

**Local extremum.** A local maximum or minimum value compared with nearby function values.

**Logarithm.** For $b>0$ and $b\ne1$, $\log_b(y)=x$ exactly when $b^x=y$.

**Logistic model.** A growth model that approaches a limiting carrying capacity, commonly written $P(t)=d/(1+ke^{-ct})$ for positive constants $c$, $d$, and $k$.

**Log-log graph.** A graph with logarithmic scales on both axes.

**Multiplicity.** The number of times a factor corresponding to a zero occurs in a polynomial.

**Observational study.** A study that records naturally occurring variables without assigning treatments.

**One-to-one function.** A function in which distinct inputs always produce distinct outputs.

**Onto function.** A function whose range equals its stated codomain.

**Parent function.** A basic function whose graph provides a starting shape for a family of related functions.

**Polynomial.** A finite sum of terms whose variable exponents are nonnegative integers.

**Population.** The complete collection of cases about which a study seeks information.

**Quadratic function.** A polynomial function $f(x)=ax^2+bx+c$ with $a\ne0$.

**Radian.** The central angle that intercepts an arc equal in length to the circle's radius.

**Range.** The set of outputs a function actually produces.

**Rational expression.** A fractional expression whose numerator and denominator are polynomials.

**Rational number.** A number that can be written as $a/b$, where $a$ and $b$ are integers and $b\ne0$.

**Real number.** A number represented by a point on the real number line. The set of all real numbers is denoted by $\mathbb{R}$.

**Root.** A value that produces a given number when raised to a specified power.

**Sample.** The subset of the population from which data are collected.

**Sample mean.** The arithmetic average $\bar x=(\sum_{i=1}^n x_i)/n$.

**Sample standard deviation.** The square root of sample variance, $s=\sqrt{\sum_{i=1}^n(x_i-\bar x)^2/(n-1)}$.

**Sampling bias.** A systematic tendency for a sampling method to overrepresent or underrepresent parts of the population.

**Semi-log graph.** A graph with one logarithmic axis and one linear axis.

**Set.** A collection of distinct objects called elements.

**Skewed distribution.** A distribution with a longer tail on one side than the other.

**Slope.** The vertical change divided by the horizontal change between two points on a nonvertical line.

**Variable.** A recorded characteristic that can differ from one case to another.

**Vertical asymptote.** A line $x=a$ approached by a function whose magnitude grows without bound as $x$ approaches $a$ from at least one side.

**Zero of a polynomial.** A value $c$ for which $P(c)=0$.
